role: Document processing and rendering across seventeen formats, identified from content rather than from a file extension. Two implementations share the repository: a zero-dependency TypeScript package for PDF in Node and the browser, and the Rust engine where new capability goes, which ships the CLI and an MCP server built for agents.

capabilities.name: doc.extract
capabilities.description: Extract what an author put in a document: text, metadata, annotations, outline, images, tables, figures, formulas, form fields, logical structure, and reading-order layout.

capabilities.name: doc.spreadsheet
capabilities.description: Read a spreadsheet as typed cells with formulas, and recompute those formulas to report what disagrees with the stored values.

capabilities.name: doc.chunk
capabilities.description: Generate semantic chunks for a retrieval pipeline.

capabilities.name: doc.search
capabilities.description: Search a document. ADF answers from the index inside the file; other formats are scanned.

capabilities.name: doc.verify
capabilities.description: Check a quotation against a document's recorded provenance, so a citation can be held to the file it claims to come from.

capabilities.name: doc.scan
capabilities.description: Scan for hidden and off-page text, which is where a document carries content a reader does not see and a model does.

capabilities.name: doc.convert
capabilities.description: Convert any supported document to Markdown, HTML, JSON or plain text.

capabilities.name: doc.displaylist
capabilities.description: Emit a page's device-space display list as JSON, for a hardware-accelerated renderer.

capabilities.name: doc.formats
capabilities.description: List every document format this build can read, with the geometry each one has and the extensions it answers to.

capabilities.name: doc.describe
capabilities.description: Emit the JSON-LD ontology an agent reads before calling anything.

capabilities.name: doc.mcp
capabilities.description: Run as an MCP stdio server, exposing the extraction surface to an agent.

unmapped.why: Everything here is about structure: what the author put in the file and where. Whether a sentence is true, relevant or an instruction aimed at a model is not asked. `doc.scan` finds text positioned where a reader will not see it, which is a fact about geometry; grading that text is IronRails' question.

unmapped.area: whether a document is safe to open
unmapped.why: A document format can carry an executing payload, and nothing here grades that. IronHardener answers what loading an artifact would do; this answers what the artifact contains.

`scanned` detects image-dominated pages that need OCR and stops there. No OCR runs, so a scanned document yields its structure and very little text, and the gap is reported rather than filled with silence.
This reads and converts. It does not author, edit or sign a document, so a conversion is a new file beside the original rather than a change to it.

The npm package handles PDF and the Rust engine handles seventeen formats. Nothing checks that both give the same answer for a PDF, so a caller choosing between them is choosing between two implementations rather than two interfaces to one.

note: Written 2026-09-14, this component's first manifest, after the rename from AgenticPDF. Capabilities are coarser than the binary's twenty-five subcommands, per IronStack decision 0006: `doc.extract` covers text, meta, annotations, outline, images, markdown, table, figures, structure, forms, formula, layout and all, because they are one capability asked about different parts of a file. `requires_grant` is false throughout except `doc.mcp`, which serves a surface to an agent rather than answering one call; nothing here holds a credential or reaches the network, and a document is read from a path the caller supplied. `budgeted` is false because the work is bounded by the file it was pointed at. The README still spells the old binary name `apdf` in fifteen places, which is why the registry carries `agenticpdf` and `apdf` as aliases.
